flawed_step: Step 3: 2-connectedness does not imply that an Euler circuit visits each vertex only once; revisiting a vertex in a chosen closed trail does not make it a cut vertex.
assessment_summary:
Attempted proof and audit:
1. Let G be an arbitrary 2-connected Eulerian graph. — Justified: this is the standard setup for proving the universal statement.
2. Since G is Eulerian, it has a closed trail W using every edge exactly once. — Justified: this is explicitly equivalent to Eulerian under the given definitions.
3. Since G is 2-connected, W cannot revisit any vertex except that its initial and final vertex coincide. — Not justified: 2-connectedness prevents a vertex deletion from disconnecting G, but it does not prevent an Euler trail from revisiting vertices.
4. Hence W is a cycle containing every vertex of G. — Not justified: the conclusion depends on the false assertion in Step 3, although every vertex does occur somewhere on W because G is connected and has no isolated vertices.
5. Therefore G is Hamiltonian. — Not justified: Step 4 has not been established.
6. Since G was arbitrary, every 2-connected Eulerian graph is Hamiltonian. — Not justified: the argument fails at Step 3.

Decisive check of falsity:
7. Let G=K_{2,4}, with bipartition classes A and B of sizes 2 and 4. — Justified: this is a finite simple graph.
8. Every vertex in A has degree 4, and every vertex in B has degree 2. — Justified: these are the degrees in K_{2,4}.
9. Thus G is connected and every vertex has even degree, so G is Eulerian. — Justified: complete bipartite graphs with two nonempty parts are connected, and Step 8 gives even degrees.
10. Deleting any one vertex leaves either K_{1,4} or K_{2,3}, both connected; hence G is 2-connected. — Justified: G has six vertices and satisfies the given vertex-deletion definition.
11. Every cycle in a bipartite graph alternates between its two parts and therefore contains equally many vertices from each part. — Justified: each edge joins opposite bipartition classes.
12. A cycle through all vertices of K_{2,4} would need to contain 2 vertices from A and 4 from B, contradicting Step 11. Thus G is not Hamiltonian. — Justified.
13. Therefore K_{2,4} is a 2-connected Eulerian graph that is not Hamiltonian, so the stated universal claim is false. — Justified.
